text: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Sydney. Which public liability lawyers are best?

result.keyword: I slipped and fell in a shopping centre in Sydney. Which public liability lawyers are best?
result.markdown:
Yes. For a **slip-and-fall in a Sydney shopping centre**, I’d focus on lawyers who regularly act in NSW public/occupiers-liability claims—not just general personal-injury firms.

I checked current 2026 sources, including Doyle’s Guide and the Law Society of NSW. Doyle’s 2026 public-liability firm rankings place **Law Partners and Slater & Gordon in its second tier**, with **Turner Freeman in its third tier**; the individual-lawyer rankings also identify several Sydney practitioners as leading or recommended public-liability lawyers. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-new-south-wales/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[lawpartners.com.au](https://lawpartners.com.au/public-liability-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/public-liability/public-liability-lawyers-in-sydney?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### My shortlist

**1. Law Partners Injury Lawyers Sydney — strong first call**

- Specifically handles **shopping-centre/supermarket slip-and-fall claims**.
- Offers a no-win-no-fee arrangement, subject to its conditions.
- Doyle’s 2026 places the firm in the **second tier** for NSW plaintiff public-liability work.
- Their Sydney office currently has a very large volume of Google reviews, though reviews shouldn't substitute for checking the actual solicitor handling your case. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-new-south-wales/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[lawpartners.com.au](https://lawpartners.com.au/public-liability-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/public-liability/public-liability-lawyers-in-sydney?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[Law Partners – public liability claims](https://lawpartners.com.au/public-liability-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**2. Slater and Gordon Lawyers — very established option**

- Has a dedicated Sydney public-liability team and specifically lists **shopping-centre slips and falls**.
- Multiple Sydney-area offices.
- No-win-no-fee arrangements are available subject to conditions.
- Doyle’s 2026 places Slater & Gordon in the **second tier** for NSW plaintiff public liability. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-new-south-wales/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[lawpartners.com.au](https://lawpartners.com.au/public-liability-lawyers?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/public-liability/public-liability-lawyers-in-sydney?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[Slater and Gordon – Sydney public liability](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/personal-injury/public-liability/public-liability-lawyers-in-sydney?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**3. Turner Freeman Lawyers Sydney — particularly worth considering**

Doyle’s 2026 identifies **Richard Dababneh and Simon Meigan of Turner Freeman as “Leading” public-liability lawyers**, and Fady Dous and Aimee Lanyon as “Recommended.” The firm itself specifically handles shopping-centre slip-and-fall claims and offers no-win-no-fee on eligible matters. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-new-south-wales/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.turnerfreeman.com.au](https://www.turnerfreeman.com.au/personal-injury-lawyers-sydney/public-liability/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[Turner Freeman – public liability](https://www.turnerfreeman.com.au/personal-injury-lawyers-sydney/public-liability/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**4. CMC Compensation Lawyers — worth getting a quote from**

CMC is particularly focused on compensation/public-liability work and says it has handled shopping-centre claims for more than 20 years. It also says it has solicitors with **Law Society of NSW Personal Injury Specialist Accreditation**. [www.cmclawyers.com.au](https://www.cmclawyers.com.au/nsw/compensation-lawyer-services/public-liability-claims?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[CMC Lawyers – public liability claims](https://www.cmclawyers.com.au/nsw/compensation-lawyer-services/public-liability-claims?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### One thing I'd do before choosing

I'd actually **speak to 2–3 of them**, rather than simply picking the firm with the highest rating. Ask:

1. **Have you handled claims against this particular shopping centre/operator?**
2. **Who will personally run my case?**
3. **What evidence do you want preserved immediately—especially CCTV?**
4. **Exactly what does “no win, no fee” cover, including disbursements and any uplift/conditional costs?**
5. **Do you think there is a viable negligence case based on the circumstances of my fall?**

The evidence can be crucial. For example, CCTV can be overwritten and the hazard itself may disappear, so acting promptly is sensible. [gwklawyers.com.au](https://gwklawyers.com.au/injury-lawyers/services-personal-injury/shopping-centre-injury-claims/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Also, don't assume that **falling automatically means the shopping centre is liable**. You generally need to establish negligence/breach of the relevant duty of care; the precise hazard, how long it existed, inspections, warnings, CCTV and your own actions can all matter. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/public-liability-compensation-lawyers-new-south-wales/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.turnerfreeman.com.au](https://www.turnerfreeman.com.au/personal-injury-lawyers-sydney/public-liability/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The Law Society's **Specialist Accreditation** is another useful filter: accredited solicitors have undergone a formal assessment of specialist competence and must maintain that accreditation. [www.lawsociety.com.au](https://www.lawsociety.com.au/for-the-public/going-court-and-working-with-lawyers/specialist-accreditation-scheme?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**If you tell me the name of the Sydney shopping centre and roughly what happened (e.g. wet floor, food spill, uneven surface, escalator, etc.), I can narrow this down to the 2–3 lawyers I'd contact first and check whether they've handled similar cases.**
